sender: Isaac Watts Monfort (via U.S. Sanitary Commission)

note: Telegram. Although a third-party message, this is the notification of ERM's Gettysburg wound; it is linked to the Gettysburg landmark waypoint. Sender confirmed by Jonathan (family historian) as Isaac Watts Monfort, brother of the recipient; a scan of the original telegram is forthcoming. Sender's identity/role confirmed as Chaplain, 52nd Indiana Infantry -- see the fuller note on the 11 July 1863 letter (entry above).

quote: I have been with Elias this day - he is better, did not think he would live for a day or two past. Have telegraphed but no word from you. He is at the house of Mr. Lightner on Baltimore Pike, 4 miles from Gettysburgh. I look for you ther - he is not with his corps.
source_file: iwm_to_jgm_18630711_gettysburg_letter.jpg / .bmp (family document, Supporting Documents and Files) -- Isaac Watts Monfort to Rev. Joseph Glass Monfort, 11 July 1863, Gettysburg; provided by Jonathan and verified against the scan
note: This is the letter that confirms ERM's stay at the Lightner Farmhouse -- previously a pending/unsourced claim on the map, now directly quoted. Signed 'Your Bro I W Monfort.' Isaac Watts Monfort's identity confirmed via the NPS Civil War Soldiers and Sailors System: Chaplain, Field & Staff, 52nd Regiment, Indiana Infantry, Union (nps.gov/civilwar UIN0052RI). Not a combat/line officer -- Union Army chaplains held only relative rank (equivalent to captain, pay grade only) and wore a plain black uniform with no rank insignia or sword. Jonathan confirmed 2026-08-08.
